title: Skull base: text study guide
reviewStatus: Source-checked teaching draft; instructor review of content and learning-objective equivalence is pending.
scope: Covers the 24 landmark annotations currently present in the external skull-base model. Paired landmarks are described together. This is not a guide to every opening or internal surface of the skull.
orientation: An inferior view looks toward the underside of the skull. Anterior means toward the face and teeth; posterior means toward the back of the head. Medial means toward the midline; lateral means away from it.
Right and left always refer to the person's anatomical right and left, not the reader's screen. Rotation changes where a feature appears on the screen, but does not change its anatomical side.

Start with the hard palate at the front and the large foramen magnum toward the back. The occipital condyles lie beside the foramen magnum. The temporal bones occupy the lateral regions of the skull base.

A foramen is an opening; a canal is a passage through bone; a fossa is a depression; a process is a projection; a condyle is an articular prominence. These words distinguish a hole from a joint surface or attachment site.
objectives: Use anatomical directions to describe a landmark relative to the midline and nearby structures.
Distinguish the hard palate, joint surfaces, projections, and passageways of the external skull base.
Compare paired right and left landmarks without relying on model colors or screen position.

entries.title: Palatine processes of the maxillae
entries.location: The anterior part of the hard palate, inside the upper dental arch.
entries.relationships: The paired processes meet at the midline. Behind them, the horizontal plates of the palatine bones complete the hard palate.
entries.significance: The hard palate separates the mouth below from the nasal cavity above.

entries.title: Horizontal plates of the palatine bones
entries.location: The posterior part of the hard palate.
entries.relationships: Each plate joins its partner at the midline and lies behind the palatine process of the maxilla on the same side.
entries.significance: Compare the posterior palatine contribution with the larger anterior maxillary contribution.

entries.title: Vomer
entries.location: At the midline of the lower portion of the bony nasal septum.
entries.relationships: It divides the nasal cavity into right and left regions; the perpendicular plate of the ethmoid contributes to the septum above it.
entries.significance: Distinguish the vertical nasal partition from the hard palate beneath the nasal cavity.
entries.sourceSection: The Nasal Septum and Nasal Conchae

entries.title: Foramen magnum
entries.location: A large midline opening in the posterior skull base.
entries.relationships: The right and left occipital condyles lie on either side of it.
entries.significance: It connects the cranial cavity and vertebral canal for the continuation of the central nervous system.

entries.title: Occipital condyles, right and left
entries.location: Paired rounded joint surfaces beside the foramen magnum.
entries.relationships: Each condyle articulates with the atlas, the first cervical vertebra, on its own side.
entries.significance: These are joint surfaces that support the skull, rather than passageways through it.

entries.title: External acoustic meatus, right and left
entries.location: The ear-canal opening on each lateral side of the skull.
entries.relationships: The mandibular fossa is in front of the opening. The mastoid process is behind the ear region.
entries.significance: Do not confuse this external opening with the internal acoustic meatus inside the cranial cavity.

entries.title: Mandibular fossae, right and left
entries.location: Depressions on the external skull base immediately anterior to the external acoustic meatus on each side.
entries.relationships: Each receives the mandibular condyle at the temporomandibular joint.
entries.significance: Identify a joint socket here, not an opening for a nerve or vessel.

entries.title: Mastoid processes, right and left
entries.location: Prominent projections that extend inferiorly behind the ear region.
entries.relationships: Compare the broad mastoid process with the slender styloid process nearby; the stylomastoid foramen lies between them.
entries.significance: The mastoid process provides an attachment site for muscles.

entries.title: Styloid processes, right and left
entries.location: Slender projections extending downward from the skull base, posterior to the mandibular fossae.
entries.relationships: The carotid canal entrance is anterior and medial to the styloid process on the same side.
entries.significance: These projections anchor small muscles and a ligament associated with the hyoid region.

entries.title: Stylomastoid foramina, right and left
entries.location: Small openings between the styloid and mastoid processes.
entries.relationships: The name combines the two surrounding projections and gives a useful location clue.
entries.significance: A cranial nerve supplying facial muscles exits here.

entries.title: Carotid canal entrances, right and left
entries.location: On the inferior skull base, anterior and medial to the styloid process on each side.
entries.relationships: The external entrance begins a tunnel through the temporal bone; it is distinct from the canal's internal exit.
entries.significance: The canal carries an artery supplying the brain.

entries.title: Jugular foramina, right and left
entries.location: Paired irregular openings at the boundary between the temporal and occipital regions of the skull base.
entries.relationships: Keep these openings distinct from the single midline foramen magnum and the nearby smooth occipital condyles.
entries.significance: They transmit cranial nerves and provide a route for venous drainage from the brain.

entries.title: Foramina ovalia, right and left
entries.location: Paired oval openings in the sphenoid region of the skull base.
entries.relationships: On each side, compare the larger foramen ovale with the smaller foramen spinosum behind and lateral to it.
entries.significance: Foramen ovale transmits the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve.

entries.title: Foramina spinosa, right and left
entries.location: Small paired openings posterior and lateral to the foramina ovalia.
entries.relationships: Use the same-side foramen ovale as the reference when locating a foramen spinosum.
entries.significance: These openings transmit a vessel supplying the cranial coverings.

practice.question: Which two sets of bones form the hard palate, and how are their contributions arranged?
practice.answer: The maxillary palatine processes form its anterior portion; the palatine horizontal plates form its posterior portion.

practice.question: How can you distinguish an occipital condyle from the foramen magnum?
practice.answer: The condyles are paired articular surfaces beside the single midline opening of the foramen magnum.

practice.question: Where is the mandibular fossa relative to the external acoustic meatus?
practice.answer: The mandibular fossa is anterior to the external acoustic meatus on the same side.

practice.question: Where is the carotid canal entrance relative to the styloid process?
practice.answer: The entrance is anterior and medial to the styloid process on the same side.

practice.question: Which opening lies between the mastoid and styloid processes?
Where is the foramen spinosum relative to the foramen ovale?
practice.answer: Posterior and lateral to the foramen ovale on the same side.
